info.title: Arcade API
info.description: Generate patterns and order them as manufactured products. Every request is a POST with a JSON body.

apiKey.description: An API key from Settings → API keys in Arcade Studio.

post.description:
Starts a job that generates a pattern from a prompt. On success, `result.patternId` is the new pattern. Jewelry prompts are checked against the selected category before a job is created; incompatible requests return HTTP 400.

Pass a `categoryId` to also make a product from the pattern. The job then runs until the product is built, and `result.productId` is the product. In a `print` category, Arcade picks the product's options. In a `jewelry` category, the pattern is a jewelry design made for that category, with options picked from the prompt; send no `modelId`, `referenceIds` or `colors`. A jewelry design is only for its own product: refines and products.create refuse it.

post.description:
Retrieves a category and its options. Not every combination of option values can be made: send the values you have decided, in any number, and each value comes back with `available`, whether some product that can be made has that value together with every value you sent for the other options.

In a `print` category, walk to any product without guessing, one call for each value you add:

1. Call with `selections: {}`. If the returned `selections` suits you, pass it to `products.create`.
2. Otherwise pick a value with `available: true` for an option you have not sent, add it to `selections`, and call again.
3. Repeat until `selections` suits you.

Choosing only available values never dead-ends, and every product that can be made is reachable in any order. If the values you send cannot be made together, `canManufacture` is `false`: the values you sent that are marked unavailable are the conflict, and the available values of those options are the ways out.

In a `jewelry` category, the options show what its products can be. patterns.create picks the values from your prompt, so name the ones you want there; products.create refuses the category.

selections.description: The values you have decided, option key to option value, in any number including none; options you leave out are open

key.description: Option key, as used in selections

available.description: Whether some product that can be made has this value together with every value you sent for the other options

selections.description: A complete selection that keeps every value you sent: each open option takes its default where that can still be made, else another available value. In a `print` category, pass it to products.create when canManufacture is true

canManufacture.description: Whether selections can be made; in a `print` category, products.create uses the lowest-priced maker that can make it. False when the values you sent cannot be made together, and selections then fills the open options with their defaults

world.description: How products in this category are made. `print`: from a pattern, by products.create or by patterns.create with this categoryId. `jewelry`: from a design made for this category, only by patterns.create with this categoryId

categoryId.description: Group ID; the categoryId of the group when it is also a category

category.description: The group this category is in, such as Rings for Dainty Diamond Ring; absent when it has none

post.description: Creates a checkout for your products. Open `checkoutUrl` to pay; the order is placed once payment completes. If any line has `quantity: 1`, set `"dropShip": true` in the request body unless you have an active subscription. Omitting `dropShip` or setting it to `false` without an active subscription returns `412 PRECONDITION_FAILED` for these lines.

post.description:
Sends a report about the API to the Arcade team: what you expected, what happened, and the request and response involved. Leave out credentials and personal data; the server also drops URL query strings, API keys and credential fields before the team sees the report.

`requestId` identifies the report. It is not an idempotency key: a retry after an error may deliver the report twice. Returns `503` while feedback is unavailable.

requestId.description: Caller-chosen ID of the report; quote it to Arcade. Not an idempotency key: a retry may deliver the report twice.

text.description: What you expected, what happened and what you tried

procedure.description: The procedure the report is about, e.g. "patterns/create"

request.description: The request the report is about

status.description: HTTP status; 0 when no response arrived

response.description: The response the report is about

agent.description: The agent or client that filed the report, e.g. "claude-code"

requestId.description: Caller-chosen ID of the report; quote it to Arcade. Not an idempotency key: a retry may deliver the report twice.
